title: Severe bleeding
keywords: bleeding blood cut wound bleed hemorrhage injury
steps: Call 112 or ask someone nearby to call.
Press firmly and directly on the wound with a clean cloth or your hand.
Do not remove soaked cloth; add more layers on top and keep pressing.
If no fracture is suspected, raise the injured limb above the heart.
Keep the person lying down and warm until help arrives.

title: Burns
keywords: burn burns burnt scald fire hot water flame
steps: Cool the burn under cool running water for 20 minutes.
Remove rings or tight items near the burn unless stuck to the skin.
Cover loosely with a clean, non-fluffy cover such as cling film.
Do not use ice, butter, toothpaste or burst blisters.
Get medical help for large burns, face, hands, chemical or electrical burns.

title: Person not breathing (CPR)
keywords: cpr unconscious breathing unresponsive collapsed heart attack cardiac arrest not breathing
steps: Check if the person responds and is breathing normally.
Call 112 and ask for an AED if one is nearby.
Push hard and fast in the centre of the chest, about 100 to 120 per minute, 5 to 6 cm deep.
Let the chest rise fully between pushes. Do not stop until help or an AED arrives.
If untrained, hands-only CPR is fine.

title: Choking
keywords: choking choke chokes stuck throat swallowed cannot breathe cough
steps: Encourage the person to keep coughing.
If they cannot cough or speak, give 5 firm back blows between the shoulder blades.
Then give 5 abdominal thrusts (stand behind, fist above the navel, pull in and up).
Alternate 5 back blows and 5 thrusts.
If the person becomes unresponsive, call 112 and start CPR.

title: Broken bone or fracture
keywords: fracture broken bone break sprain twisted swelling leg arm limb
steps: Do not move the person unless there is immediate danger.
Keep the injured part still; support it with padding or a splint.
Do not try to straighten the bone.
Control any bleeding with gentle pressure around the wound.
Get medical help; keep the person warm and calm.

title: Drowning and flood rescue
keywords: drowning drown water flood river swept rescue swimming
steps: Do not enter moving water. Throw a rope, float or bottle to the person.
Call 112 and get them out safely.
Check breathing. If not breathing, start CPR with rescue breaths if trained.
Keep the person warm and on their side if breathing.
Take them to a hospital even if they seem fine.

title: Heatstroke
keywords: heat heatstroke sun hot dizzy faint temperature dehydration
steps: Move the person to shade or a cool place.
Cool the body with wet cloths, water and fanning, especially neck, armpits and groin.
Give small sips of water only if fully alert.
Call 112 if the person is confused, vomiting or unconscious.

title: Snake bite
steps: Keep the person calm and still.
Immobilise the bitten limb and keep it at or below heart level.
Remove rings and tight items near the bite.
Do not cut, suck, apply ice or tie a tight tourniquet.
Go to a hospital immediately for anti-venom.

title: Earthquake safety
keywords: earthquake quake tremor shaking building collapse aftershock
steps: Drop, Cover and Hold On under a sturdy table. Stay away from windows.
If outdoors, move away from buildings, wires and trees.
After shaking stops, check for injuries and expect aftershocks.
Avoid damaged buildings and do not use matches if you smell gas.

title: Flood safety
keywords: flood flooding rain water rising landslide cyclone storm evacuate
steps: Move to higher ground immediately.
Do not walk or drive through floodwater.
Switch off electricity at the mains only if it is safe to do so.
Keep away from fallen power lines.
Boil or treat drinking water before use.

title: Electric shock
keywords: electric shock electrocution current wire power live
steps: Do not touch the person until the power is off.
Switch off at the mains, or push the source away with a dry wooden or plastic object.
Call 112. Check breathing and start CPR if not breathing.
Treat burns by cooling with running water.

title: Fainting or unconscious but breathing
keywords: faint fainted unconscious passed out unresponsive recovery position
steps: Check that the person is breathing.
If breathing, place them on their side (recovery position).
Loosen tight clothing and do not give food or drink.
Call 112 if they do not wake up within a minute.
